scenes.title: Tunisie, Carthage, le cirque
scenes.description: A press photograph from 1912 by Agence Rol shows the circus at Carthage. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie.
scenes.explanation: The lightweight X-frame folding camp stool with a fabric seat did not exist in 1912, so it cannot belong to this excavation scene.

scenes.title: aviateur René Paulhan
scenes.description: A press photograph from May 1934 by the Agence Meurisse shows the aviator René Paulhan, who lived from 1907 to 1937, with biplanes. The negative on glass is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie.
scenes.explanation: The plastic cable tie was patented in 1958, so it could not exist on an aircraft photographed in 1934.

scenes.title: 22-12-12, Saint-Cloud, Paul Meyer [à cheval]
scenes.description: A press photograph taken by Agence Rol on 22 December 1912 at Saint-Cloud shows Paul Meyer on horseback. The record identifies it as a glass negative held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
scenes.explanation: The hard-shell ventilated bicycle helmet did not exist in 1912; it became common only in the 1970s.

scenes.title: 2/3/31, pari mutuel urbain [les parieurs]
scenes.description: A 1931 press photograph by Agence Rol shows bettors at the pari-mutuel urbain in Paris. The glass negative, held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, is dated 2 March 1931 and concerns horse-race gambling in Paris.
scenes.explanation: Contactless payment terminals did not exist in 1931, so a card reader on this box-office counter is impossible for the scene.

scenes.title: 15-4-11, inspection sanitaire à la Villette [nettoyage des enclos]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol dated 15 April 1911 shows a sanitary inspection at La Villette in Paris, specifically the cleaning of the enclosures. The record identifies the subject as the Marché et abattoirs de la Villette (La Villette market and slaughterhouses) and the disinfection of slaughterhouses in Paris.
scenes.explanation: Cordless power tools with rechargeable battery packs did not exist in 1911, as the first practical cordless drills appeared in the 1960s.
